title: Tren del Sur: Tenerife's Long-Awaited Rail Dream

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Alright Mia, let's talk about something that's been a dream — and a frustration — for people on this island for a very long time. The Tren del Sur.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Yes! And for anyone who's sat in bumper-to-bumper traffic on the TF-1 trying to get from Costa Adeje up to Santa Cruz, this one is personal.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: So let's set the scene. Right now, Tenerife has zero rail. None. If you're staying in the south — Los Cristianos, Costa Adeje — and you need to get to the airport or all the way up to Santa Cruz, you're on a TITSA bus or in a car, and at peak times that motorway can be genuinely painful.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Which is why the Tren del Sur has been talked about for so long. The proposal is an 80-kilometre standard-gauge electrified railway connecting the Santa Cruz Transport Interchange all the way down to Adeje — that's Tenerife's fourth-largest town — with five stations in between.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: And crucially, a stop at Tenerife South Airport. Which, believe it or not, wasn't always guaranteed. But in 2026, the Cabildo de Tenerife and Aena — Spain's airport operator — finally reached a formal agreement to include that station. Island president Rosa Dávila called it the final administrative step needed to move the whole project forward.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: That's genuinely significant. An airport without a rail link in 2026 feels like a real gap. But Alex, I do want to pump the brakes slightly — because this project has a *history*.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Oh, it does. It was shelved indefinitely back in 2011 for economic reasons, then reactivated in 2017. So we're talking about more than a decade of discussions, delays, and restarts.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: And the budget reflects that stop-start history. It's now sitting at €2.5 billion — that's €700 million more than the previous estimate. So it's not a small ask.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Right. Though the Cabildo has put €1 million in its 2026 budget to refine the exact route through the airport area and design the transport interchange. So the wheels are turning, even if slowly.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: The current timeline has construction going out to tender between late 2027 and early 2028. No firm groundbreaking date yet.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Which is where I'd say... cautious optimism is the right mood. The airport agreement is real progress. The budget allocation is real progress. But given the history, I think locals and expats are wise not to book their first train journey just yet.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Agreed. But if this does get built — and I genuinely hope it does — it transforms how this island moves. For tourists, for workers commuting along the south coast, for anyone trying to get off a plane without queuing for a taxi.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: It would be a game changer. Let's just hope 2027 doesn't become 2031. We'll be watching this one closely — and we'd love to hear what you think. Should Tenerife finally get its train? Find us online at Radio Tenerify.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: More to come on this. Stay with us.
